# Dedicated funds: year-by-year balances

*Generated by `index/tools/funds-model.py` (run by `run-all.sh`); do not edit by hand. Inputs: `index/data/inputs/funds-*.csv` (the 2026 Trustees tables and this model's parameters), the ledger, the long-term fiscal model and the transportation model from the same run.*

> **Education adoption update:** This is the preserved pre-EDU-9B numerical comparison. Espen has adopted the full education-fund benefit scope and payroll institution. Use [the integrated education and fiscal recovery bridge](fiscal-recovery-model.md) for current selected-scope costs and conditional financing. Old “held education” and “decided package” labels below describe the earlier vintage; they do not reverse that adoption or establish a current financing/D3/D4 pass. Exact new rates and transition finance await decision.

> **Climate integration disclosure:** CLI-7C carries $75–150B of contingent exposure, not scored; its expected cost is included in the common fiscal model. The carbon table below is the preserved $150 baseline; Package A process/combustion increments and O5 routing are in the common ledger and recovery audit.

The general-fund ledger counts only general-fund money. This file follows the funds it leaves out: Social Security and Medicare HI over 75 years, the paid-leave fund, the Highway Trust Fund's three accounts, the carbon channel, and the held education fund (EDU-9B). Dollar figures are nominal; ten-year sums are 2030-39 in trillions.

## Social Security (D8)

**Check against the Trustees.** Run on the 2026 Trustees' intermediate rates, the model puts combined-fund depletion in **2034** with **83%** of benefits payable, and the 75-year actuarial balance at **-4.45%** of taxable payroll. The Trustees report 2034, 83% and −4.42% (sourced). The model's balance is the Trustees' summarized-rate formula on their annual rates, so a small difference is rounding in the published rates and the interest path.

**How the provisions are evaluated.** Each D8 provision is applied on its face (its rate, threshold, start year and benefit credit) to a tax base taken from SSA's single-year scores of the same kind of provision on the 2026 Trustees' assumptions (`funds-ss-ssa-runs.csv`, sourced). Earnings above the taxable maximum come from SSA's E2.1; thresholds above the maximum follow a Pareto tail fitted to E2.5 ($250K) and E2.17 ($400K) (fitted exponent 1.83); the maximum is $184,500 in 2026 and passes $250,000 in 2034, after which SS-1 taxes all earnings. Investment income above an unindexed threshold comes from F11 ($400K) and F9 (ACA thresholds); active pass-through income from F8. The benefit credit's cost comes from E2.14, CPI-E's from A6 and the minimum benefit's from B5.2, each moved to the D8 start year. SSA's behavioral responses are inside those bases. Interactions between provisions are ignored (SSA's F10, which taxes investment and pass-through income together at $400K, scores 1.81 against F11 plus F8's 2.15, so stacking SS-2 and SS-5 likely overstates them by up to a few tenths of a point).

**Check: SSA's own provisions rebuilt from the same bases** (75-year change in the actuarial balance, % of payroll):

| E2.17: 12.4% above $400K, 2027, no credit | +2.32 | +2.33 | -0.01 |
| E2.14: 12.4% above $250K, 2028, 2% credit | +2.40 | +2.41 | -0.01 |
| F11: 12.4% on investment income above $400K, 2028 | +1.22 | +1.22 | -0.00 |
| F9: 12.4% on investment income, ACA thresholds, 2028 | +1.31 | +1.32 | -0.01 |
| F8: active pass-through income, 2027 | +0.93 | +0.93 | +0.00 |
| A6: CPI-E COLA from Dec 2028 | -0.35 | -0.33 | -0.02 |

| Scenario | Depletion | Payable then | 75-year balance | Share of the gap closed | Sustainable solvency | Trust fund ratio 2040 / 2060 / 2080 / 2100 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Current law | 2034 | 83% | -4.45 | 0% | no | 0% / 0% / 0% / 0% |
| D8 baseline | 2062 | 90% | -1.60 | 64% | no | 80% / 20% / 0% / 0% |
| D8 + SS-5 | 2081 | 86% | -0.73 | 84% | no | 128% / 181% / 15% / 0% |

**Reading.** Evaluated on their face, the D8 baseline closes about 64% of the 75-year gap and moves depletion from 2034 to 2062; with SS-5 it closes 84% and depletion moves to 2081. The new taxes are large from their first year: SS-1 alone adds about 2.3% of payroll in 2031, against a current-law shortfall of about 2.6%. The trust fund ratio is the reserve at the start of a year over that year's cost; 'sustainable' means no depletion through 2100 and a ratio of at least 100% that is not falling at the end, a conservative model criterion (the Trustees require positive reserves and a stable or rising terminal ratio; the one-year minimum here is additional). These are estimates built from SSA's scores of each provision alone; an SSA score of the package would replace them. SS-10 (the bipartisan trade) is not modeled; it needs an SSA score of its pieces.

## Medicare HI (summary level)

Rates are the 2026 Trustees' HI cost and income rates at the years they publish, interpolated between (sourced); HI's taxable payroll is taken as 1.25 times OASDI's because it is uncapped (estimate). **Check:** the model puts depletion in **2034** with 89% payable and a 75-year balance of **-0.64%**, against the Trustees' 2033, 89% and −0.56% (sourced).

**With the program.** HI's sources in the program are REV-H1a ($0.5T) and HLT-6's Part A share ($0.7T, estimate), $1.20T in 2030-39, held at the same share of HI payroll after 2039 (estimate). They improve the 75-year balance by **+0.60%** of HI payroll, against the Trustees' 0.56% gap, so they close it on this reading; on the model's own rates HI then depletes in 2064 and the balance is -0.04%. Because the model's current-law balance is -0.08 points off the Trustees', the gain (not the model's absolute balance) is the reading to use; a year-by-year Trustees HI table would sharpen it.

## Paid leave (FAM-3)

The contribution starts at 0.60% of covered payroll in 2030 (Trustees' taxable payroll used as the base, estimate) and benefits start in 2031, ramping over 2 years. Benefit cost is set so 2030-39 benefits match the ledger's FAM-3 range ($0.6T / $0.9T / $1.4T). The rule: when the reserve is below 1 year of next year's benefits the rate steps up 0.05 points the next January, to 0.85%; above 1.5 years it steps back down; a shortfall at the cap is a Treasury loan repaid with interest.

**Check:** at 0.60% the contribution raises $0.97T in 2030-39 (ledger P1: $0.90T) and $1.37T at the cap (ledger: $1.28T).

| Take-up case | Mature cost (% of payroll) | First step-up | Rate 2035 / 2039 / 2050 | Receipts 2030-39 | Benefits 2030-39 | Treasury loan owed 2039 / 2050 ($B) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| low | 0.43% | never | 0.60% / 0.60% / 0.60% | $0.97T | $0.60T | 0 / 0 |
| mid | 0.65% | 2039 | 0.60% / 0.65% / 0.60% | $0.98T | $0.90T | 0 / 0 |
| high | 1.01% | 2032 | 0.80% / 0.85% / 0.85% | $1.23T | $1.40T | 184 / 865 |

**Reading.** At low and middle take-up the fund pays its way at or near 0.60%. At high take-up the mature cost (1.01% of payroll) is above the 0.85% cap, so the loan never stops growing: the bridge is not temporary in that case, and a design choice is needed (a higher cap, a benefit adjustment, or the general-fund backstop FAM-3E). In the window the loan reaches $184B (the domain file's about $120B, estimate).

## Highway Trust Fund (Moving America)

From the transportation model (`transportation/moving_america.py`, Draft 2's design): each account's dedicated receipts against its program, the general-fund top-up where receipts fall short, and receipts trapped in an account above its program. $B by fiscal year.

| FY | Highway: receipts / program / top-up | Transit: receipts / program / top-up | Rail: receipts / program / top-up | Trapped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2029 | 43 / 77 / 34 | 7 / 24 / 17 | 0 / 18 / 18 | 0 |
| 2030 | 46 / 78 / 32 | 11 / 33 / 22 | 1 / 30 / 28 | 0 |
| 2031 | 51 / 80 / 28 | 17 / 36 / 19 | 3 / 39 / 36 | 0 |
| 2032 | 55 / 84 / 29 | 21 / 40 / 19 | 8 / 40 / 32 | 0 |
| 2034 | 64 / 92 / 28 | 31 / 44 / 14 | 14 / 52 / 38 | 0 |
| 2036 | 74 / 101 / 27 | 41 / 48 / 7 | 21 / 59 / 38 | 0 |
| 2038 | 91 / 106 / 14 | 43 / 52 / 9 | 25 / 43 / 18 | 0 |
| 2040 | 101 / 111 / 10 | 49 / 56 / 7 | 30 / 43 / 13 | 0 |
| 2042 | 109 / 117 / 8 | 54 / 60 / 6 | 37 / 48 / 11 | 0 |
| 2044 | 118 / 123 / 5 | 60 / 64 / 4 | 43 / 48 / 6 | 0 |
| 2046 | 124 / 129 / 5 | 64 / 68 / 4 | 44 / 48 / 5 | 0 |

Where an account's receipts fall short of its program, the gap is a general-fund top-up, counted in the ledger (MOV-29, MOV-30 and the later-Congress MOV-31), so no account runs a deficit; the top-ups shrink to $14B in FY2046. Programs here include expansion; on renewal alone, FY2042-46 receipts cover 95% of highway, 109% of transit and 135% of rail renewal (the transportation model). D4 requires the Highway Trust Fund to remain whole for 75 years. This model stops in 2046 and does not establish that test; renewal coverage in the 2040s is evidence for that period only. Expansion still draws on the general fund.

## Carbon channel (D7)

REV-C1 ($1.90T) spread over 2030-39 on the fee's durability path (price times a falling emissions index, the C1 profile in `incidence-phase-in.csv`); REV-C2 ($0.03T) on the same path. 80% of C1 is the dividend (CLI-2), the rest the transition share (to CLI-5). The dividend is equal per adult (CLI-2A); it uses a population of 346 million in 2030 growing 0.4% a year, 78% of it adults (estimates).

## Historical education-fund comparison (pre-adoption)

Historical comparison: Espen subsequently adopted the full EDU-9B scope and payroll institution. These estate-funded cases are retained as the prior calculation, not current financing. Use fiscal-recovery-model.md. The fund is modeled as the session designed it: an uncapped payroll contribution ($135B a point in 2030, growing 4% a year), an estate component growing 5% a year, and the session's spending path ($142B in 2030 to $442B in 2049, $2.60T in 2030-39). Reserves earn the trust-fund rate. The rate needed is the lowest that keeps the reserve at or above zero through 2049 without borrowing.

| Estate component | Rate needed (points) | At 1.28: trough / reserve 2049 ($B) | At 1.40: trough / reserve 2049 ($B) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 counted ($0.35T) | 1.38 | -509 (2049) / -509 | +56 (2039) / +210 |
| E1's new money only ($0.15T) | 1.50 | -1283 (2049) / -1283 | -564 (2049) / -564 |

The domain file estimates about 1.4 points with REV-E1 counted, and slightly above with only its new money (estimate). General-fund relief if taken up: FAM-2, EDU-1, EDU-3 and EDU-4 leave the general fund, $1.23T in 2030-39 on the long-term model's rows (domain file: $1.23T), plus the current spending the fund absorbs (about $0.77T, estimate).
